title: Discuss, explain, depend on
goal: Use the right preposition after common verbs, or none at all
intro: Many verbs come with a fixed preposition: depend on, listen to, wait for, married to. Others take none, though we often add one from habit: discuss (not discuss about), explain something to someone (not explain me), return (not return back). These patterns make a big difference to how natural you sound.

rules.rule: Fixed pairs: depend on, listen to, wait for, look for, belong to, agree with, married to, good at, afraid of, interested in.
No preposition: discuss, reach, attend, answer, marry, request, emphasize.
explain / describe / say something TO someone.
examples: Can you explain it to me?

mistakes.right: Can you explain this to me?

mistakes.wrong: He is married with my cousin.
mistakes.right: He is married to my cousin.

ex.q: I’ve been waiting ___ you for an hour!

ex.fixed: Please explain the process to me.

ex.q: My sister is married with an engineer.
ex.fixed: My sister is married to an engineer.

ex.a: Can you describe the problem to me?

ex.q: Correct this: “Can you explain me the meaning?”
a: Can you explain the meaning to me

talk: Talk about a problem at work or home: what you discussed, who explained things to you, what it depends on, and who you’re waiting for.
